title: Accommodation-engineered argon backside cooling replaces helium wafer chucks
idea: Effect: free-molecular (Knudsen) gas conduction scales with alpha/(2-alpha)*P/sqrt(M), and helium's accommodation coefficient on smooth ceramic is only ~0.3 while argon's is ~0.8-0.9. Redesign electrostatic chucks with a 3-5 um gap, nano-textured Al2O3 mesas and stronger sealing bands so Ar/N2 runs at 2-3x the pressure while staying free-molecular, matching helium heat-transfer coefficients.
why: Helium chokepoint (Qatar ~30% offline): backside cooling is one of the largest fab helium uses; target ~100% He removal on etch/deposition chucks with <15% throughput penalty.

title: Johnsen-Rahbek solid-contact chucks remove backside gas entirely
idea: Effect: the Johnsen-Rahbek effect concentrates the clamping field across micro-gaps of a slightly conductive dielectric, giving ~10x the clamp force of a Coulomb chuck. Pair it with a compliant AlN-nanocomposite top layer so heat leaves through >30% real solid contact area instead of gas, and tune temperature uniformity with zoned JR voltages.
why: Helium: eliminates the backside-gas loop and its leak points; contact conductance >1000 W/m2K, comparable to He-gas cooling at the ~10 Torr typical of etch tools.

title: Cold-crucible induction skull melting gives quartz-free Czochralski silicon
idea: Effect: eddy-current induction heats silicon inside a segmented, water-cooled copper crucible while the Lorentz force pushes the melt off the wall, so molten Si rests on its own frozen Si skull and never touches fused quartz; add a cusp magnetic field to damp convection while pulling 300 mm crystals.
why: High-purity quartz crucibles (Spruce Pine >80%): removes about one crucible per ingot and most oxygen contamination, at roughly +30-50% melt energy.

title: Non-wetting nitride crucibles exploit molten silicon contact-angle physics
idea: Effect: molten Si wets and dissolves silica but beads up (contact angle >90 deg) on dense reaction-bonded Si3N4 or CVD-SiC. Make crucibles from nitrogen and metallurgical silicon with a renewable nitride release coat; the light nitrogen doping it adds is the same doping already used to strengthen CZ wafers.
why: Quartz chokepoint: crucible feedstock becomes N2 plus metallurgical Si, which the U.S. can produce; crucible could be reused 5-10 pulls instead of once.

title: Orbital Hall torque from titanium and oxidized copper, no heavy metals
idea: Effect: the orbital Hall effect makes orbital angular-momentum currents in light metals (Ti, Cr, Cu/CuOx) with Hall conductivity rivaling Pt spin Hall. A Ti or Cu/CuOx channel plus a thin Ni orbital-to-spin conversion layer switches an MTJ free layer, building SOT-MRAM working memory with no Pt, W or Ta.
why: Scarce-metal intensity (W China ~80%, Ta conflict mineral, Pt): SOT-MRAM gives ~1-5 ns, no refresh and >1e14 endurance; if orbital torque efficiency reaches ~0.5, switching current is ~3-5x lower than with W.

title: Size-effect-optimized NiAl intermetallic wordlines replace buried tungsten
idea: Effect: Fuchs-Sondheimer surface and Mayadas-Shatzkes grain-boundary scattering penalize long-mean-free-path metals below 20 nm. B2-ordered NiAl and CuAl2 have ~5 nm electron mean free paths and need no TiN barrier, so at 10-15 nm widths they match or beat W+TiN. Co-sputter or ALD the layers, then order them with a short anneal.
why: Tungsten (China ~80%) and WF6 fluorine chemistry; reclaiming barrier volume gives 20-40% lower wordline RC, and Ni and Al are widely sourced.

title: Template-stabilized rutile titania reaches k near 100 without hafnium
idea: Effect: rutile TiO2 has k ~80-170 but normally forms low-k anatase. ALD it onto a lattice-matched rutile-structure conductor (Sb:SnO2 or MoO2 instead of scarce Ru) so epitaxial templating locks in rutile, and use Al doping at grain boundaries to plug leakage.
why: Capacitor charge wall (needs k~70) and Zr/Hf dependence: ~2x Cs at the same aspect ratio, or AR cut from ~70 to ~35, which also cuts fluorocarbon etch time; Ti is the 9th most abundant element.

title: Spin-crossover iron complexes store bits inside thermal hysteresis loops
idea: Effect: Fe(II)-triazole coordination polymers switch between low-spin and high-spin states with a 20-40 K wide thermal hysteresis loop near room temperature. Nano-cells held at the loop center are flipped by a local Joule pulse and read through their 10-30% change in permittivity or conductance; there is no stored charge to leak.
why: Refresh (fact 3) and Hf/W/capacitor-etch dependence; uses only Fe, C, N, H, so no scarce element is involved.

title: Coulomb-blockade silicon nanodots hold countable electrons in all-silicon cells
idea: Effect: a 5 nm Si nanodot has a charging energy well above kT, so Coulomb blockade adds an escape barrier on top of the SiO2 tunnel barrier. Store ~10-30 electrons by direct tunneling and read them with an adjacent room-temperature single-electron-transistor charge sensor; the cell needs only Si, SiO2 and doped-Si wiring.
why: Removes the capacitor (facts 1-2), high-k and W; the tiny stored charge gives ~100x lower CV2 write energy.

title: Resonant-tunneling Goto-pair latch built from silicon and oxide only
idea: Effect: negative differential resistance in two series Si/SiO2 (or Si/CaF2) double-barrier resonant-tunneling diodes makes a bistable midpoint node (Goto pair) that holds a bit at nA standby with no capacitor. One access transistor completes a ~3-device static cell, with no III-V and no Ge.
why: Capacitor elimination and refresh-free operation; the cell is ~2-3x DRAM area but needs no high-AR capacitor etch or high-k, so tool capital per wafer drops.

title: Strain-switched iron-aluminum nanomagnets on AlN, magnetoelectric memory
idea: Effect: inverse magnetostriction. A voltage across a sputtered AlN piezo layer strains an Fe-Al (Alfenol) nanomagnet and rotates its easy axis to toggle the bit for ~1 fJ, read through MgO tunnel magnetoresistance. Avoids Ga (Galfenol), Sc (ScAlN), Co, and the Pt/Ir/Ru of SOT and pinning stacks.
why: Energy per bit (voltage floor, fact 10) and scarce-element intensity: ~100x lower write energy than STT-MRAM, using abundant Fe, Al and N.

title: LNG regasification cold runs a 77 K refresh-free memory tier
idea: Effect: thermally activated junction and GIDL leakage collapse at 77 K, stretching DRAM retention from 64 ms to hours. Build cryo-memory pods at LNG import terminals, where regasification throws away ~830 kJ of cold per kg, and cool commodity DRAM with liquid-nitrogen loops (never helium) at re-centered voltages.
why: Refresh energy (16-33% of idle power) nearly eliminated, lower VARY possible, helium-free cryogenics, and wasted industrial cold reused as a power source.

title: Mn3Sn antiferromagnet bits switched by Neel-order spin-orbit torque
idea: Effect: the noncollinear antiferromagnet Mn3Sn has a large anomalous Hall effect and tunnel magnetoresistance despite near-zero net moment. Switch its octupole order with current pulses and read it through Mn3Sn/MgO/Mn3Sn junctions, which removes IrMn pinning, Ru spacers and Pt torque layers.
why: Removes Ir, Ru and Pt (ultra-scarce PGMs) from magnetic memory; zero stray field allows denser packing, and ps-scale dynamics are possible; Mn and Sn are mined on several continents.

title: Pyroelectric non-destructive readout of boron-aluminum-nitride ferroelectric cells
idea: Effect: pyroelectricity. Store bits in wurtzite Al(1-x)B(x)N ferroelectric capacitors (no Hf, no Sc) and read them without switching: a ~5 K heat pulse from a wordline micro-heater makes a pyro-current whose sign gives the polarization. Because the signal is only hundreds of electrons, an in-cell gain transistor senses it.
why: Destructive read (fact 8) and Hf/Sc dependence: endurance is limited only by writes, and Al, B and N are abundant and U.S.-sourced.

title: Photoacoustic isotope-tracer leak detection retires helium mass spectrometers
idea: Effect: photoacoustics. A modulated mid-IR laser absorbed by a 13CO2 tracer gas creates pressure waves that a resonant MEMS microphone detects at ppb levels. 13CO2 has almost no background, so it replaces helium spraying for leak-checking vacuum chambers, gas lines and EUV/etch tools.
why: Helium: leak testing is a top-3 fab helium use; equivalent sensitivity is reached with a recyclable, abundant tracer.

title: Hollow-fiber sieving plus pressure swing recaptures fab helium as service
idea: Effect: helium's 2.6 angstrom kinetic diameter lets it permeate polyimide hollow fibers ~100x faster than N2 or Ar. Capture exhaust at chucks, load locks and leak stations, enrich it to 90% through membranes, finish it to 5N by pressure-swing adsorption and refill on site, all sold as helium-as-a-service.
why: Helium chokepoint: 70-90% recovery cuts virgin helium purchases ~5-10x and protects fabs from Qatar-type outages.

title: Talbot self-imaging prints periodic memory arrays without EUV
idea: Effect: Talbot self-imaging. DRAM arrays are strictly periodic, so displacement Talbot lithography (a simple phase grating lit at 193 nm and integrated across the Talbot distance) prints pitch-halved lines and honeycomb hole arrays with no complex reticle. Self-aligned quadruple patterning then reaches array pitch, and only the periphery uses conventional litho.
why: EUV single-supplier chokepoint and 5-7 EUV layers (fact 4): the array layers move to tools at ~1/10 EUV capex with mask cost near zero.

title: Unseparated zirconium-hafnium precursors exploit lanthanide-contraction chemical twins
idea: Effect: lanthanide contraction gives Zr4+ and Hf4+ nearly identical radii and dielectric chemistry, so ZrO2 capacitor layers and HfO2 gate layers tolerate natural 1-3% cross-content. Write a SEMI/JEDEC spec for separation-free Zr(Hf) precursors made directly from zircon sand, skipping the nuclear-grade solvent-extraction plants where hafnium supply is concentrated.
why: Hafnium (~70 t/yr from a few refiners): supply opens to all zircon miners (Australia, South Africa, U.S.) and precursor cost falls.

title: Supercritical CO2 rinsing eliminates surface tension and ultrapure water
idea: Effect: above its critical point (31 C, 74 bar) CO2 has zero surface tension and liquid-like solvating power. Post-etch residue removal and drying of 70:1 capacitor pillars runs in recycled sCO2 with a cosolvent instead of UPW rinse and IPA dry, so capillary forces cannot collapse the pillars.
why: Water intensity (several m3 UPW per wafer) and the pillar-collapse limit on capacitor aspect ratio (fact 1), allowing taller capacitors.

title: Molten-salt electro-deoxidation turns ordinary sand into domestic silicon feedstock
idea: Effect: field-driven oxide-ion migration. In the FFC-Cambridge process O2- ions leave a SiO2 cathode into molten CaCl2 at ~850 C, leaving porous silicon with no carbothermic arc furnace or chlorosilane Siemens reactor; directional solidification and segregation refining then push purity toward CZ feedstock grade.
why: Polysilicon concentration (China ~90%) and Siemens energy (~50-60 kWh/kg): targets <20 kWh/kg from any sand at U.S. sites.

title: Capacitive deionization loops recycle dilute fab rinse water cheaply
idea: Effect: electric-double-layer electrosorption. Activated-carbon electrodes pull ions out of dilute rinse streams with energy that scales with the ions removed, unlike RO, which scales with water volume. Cascade CDI and EDI to return >90% of rinse water to the UPW plant, and recover energy on discharge.
why: Water and energy intensity of DRAM fabs: 2-3x lower purification energy for dilute streams and a large cut in fresh-water draw.

title: Band-to-band tunneling access transistors flatten the retention leakage tail
idea: Effect: quantum band-to-band tunneling. Replace the thermionic access FET with an all-silicon tunnel FET whose off-state leakage is set by tunneling, giving aA/um levels that barely depend on temperature. The weak-cell tail vanishes, and the low on-current is fine because charging 5 fF at 1 uA takes only ~5 ns.
why: Access-transistor leakage tail (fact 3): refresh intervals 10-100x longer cut refresh energy and bandwidth loss; Si-only, with no Ge or III-V.

title: LC-resonant adiabatic wordline drive recycles charge energy
idea: Effect: adiabatic charging, where loss is about (RC/T)*CV2. Drive wordlines from a resonant sinusoidal supply through on-interposer inductors so the 3 V swing ramps slowly relative to RC, and return the charge to the LC tank instead of dumping it to ground.
why: Voltage floor (fact 10): wordline energy falls ~70%, which cuts the energy intensity of every activation.

title: Self-ordered anodic alumina pores as etch-free capacitor molds
idea: Effect: field-assisted ion migration during room-temperature aluminum anodization self-organizes hexagonal pores with aspect ratios >1000:1. A coarse nanoimprint pre-pattern registers them, and ALD TiN/dielectric/TiN at <=300 C fills them, so no high-AR plasma etch is needed. Every step stays below 400 C.
why: PFAS/fluorocarbon etch gases (C4F6, C4F8) and capital-heavy etchers; AR ~150:1 pushes Cs toward ~10 fF, breaking the capacitor wall (fact 1).

title: Indium- and gallium-free zinc-tin oxide gain cells under 350 C
idea: Effect: conduction through overlapping spherical Sn 5s / Zn 4s orbitals keeps amorphous Zn-Sn-O a good semiconductor, and its ~3.3 eV gap suppresses thermal generation to ~1e-19 A/um. Sputter ZTO at room temperature and anneal it at <=350 C to build 2T0C gain cells stacked in BEOL.
why: Scarce-element intensity of oxide memory: removes In (China ~60%) and Ga (China ~98%), with retention >100 s for ~1000x lower refresh energy.

title: Croconic acid ferroelectric memory built only from carbon, hydrogen, oxygen
idea: Effect: croconic acid switches polarization (~20 uC/cm2, close to BaTiO3) by collective proton transfer along hydrogen-bonded chains at room temperature. Vacuum-sublime oriented films below 150 C as the last BEOL step and use them as the ferroelectric in FeFET or 1T-1C working memory.
why: Replaces Hf/Zr ferroelectrics and fluorinated PVDF (PFAS); a low coercive field allows sub-1 V writes; supply risk is zero because the element set is C, H and O.

title: Light-addressed photoconductive access through silicon-nitride waveguide wordlines
idea: Effect: photoconductivity. A PECVD SiN waveguide grid (300 C) replaces metal wordlines, and each cell's access device is a microcrystalline-Si photoconductor (PECVD 250 C). A laser pulse into one row's waveguide turns its photoconductors on (on/off ~1e5) while dark cells isolate their storage nodes.
why: Tungsten wordlines, wordline-driver periphery (fact 7) and row hammer (fact 9, since there is no electrical wordline coupling); all layers are BEOL-compatible.

title: Autocatalytic electroless plating fills contacts at 80 C without WF6
idea: Effect: autocatalytic reduction. A DMAB-reduced Ni-B film nucleates directly on TiN and acts as a liner for bottom-up electroless Cu, filling high-AR contacts and buried lines void-free in aqueous baths at <90 C, replacing CVD tungsten from WF6.
why: Tungsten (China ~80%), fluorine chemistry and CVD tool cost; ~5x lower line resistivity than W at contact dimensions, with a bath far below 400 C.

title: Aluminum-induced layer exchange grows poly-silicon access transistors at 350 C
idea: Effect: amorphous Si dissolves into Al grain boundaries and crystallizes underneath at ~350 C, swapping layer order (layer exchange) to give >10 um grains with no Ni, laser or furnace. Strip the Al, thin and counter-dope the film, and build stacked BEOL access and periphery transistors over the array.
why: Single-crystal wafer intensity (quartz crucibles, polysilicon) and 3D tier cost (fact 2): extra silicon tiers come from abundant Al and silane under 400 C.

title: Stressor-driven controlled spalling reuses one CZ wafer twenty times
idea: Effect: fracture mechanics. A tensile Ni stressor film plated at room temperature drives a crack parallel to the surface at a depth set by film stress (Suo-Hutchinson mode mixity), peeling 10-20 um single-crystal Si layers without kerf. Bond them to carriers at <=300 C for junctionless accumulation-mode cell transistors, re-polish the donor and repeat; sold as a wafer-leasing model.
why: Quartz crucible and polysilicon intensity per device layer fall ~10-20x, and every step stays at room temperature to 300 C.

title: Deep-UV photochemical activation forms oxide dielectrics at 150 C
idea: Effect: photolysis. 185/254 nm UV breaks sol-gel ligands and makes ozone and atomic oxygen in situ, condensing dense M-O-M networks of AlOx and ZrOx from spin-coated or inkjet precursors at <=150 C. This replaces furnace and ALD steps for storage-node and gate dielectrics in stacked tiers.
why: Energy and vacuum-tool capital; removes the thermal budget that drives quartz furnace consumables; printable dielectrics cut capital intensity for oxide memory tiers.

title: HiPIMS-grown VO2 Mott latches hold bits inside hysteresis windows
idea: Effect: the Mott insulator-metal transition has an electrically driven hysteresis window. High-power impulse magnetron sputtering supplies energetic ions so monoclinic VO2 (Cr-doped to move the transition above 85 C operating temperature) crystallizes at <=300 C. A VO2 element biased inside its window latches as a one-resistor static bit switched by ns pulses.
why: Removes capacitor, high-k and W from the cell; vanadium has U.S. sources (Utah, Arkansas) and the whole process is BEOL-compatible below 400 C.

title: Euler-buckled silicon-nitride nanobeams store bits as snap-through states
idea: Effect: Euler buckling bistability. A PECVD SiN beam deposited at 300 C with built-in compressive stress buckles up or down, two states separated by a barrier much larger than kT. Electrostatic electrodes snap it through in ~10 ns (GHz-class stiffness at sub-um length), and capacitive sensing reads its position; tiers stack in BEOL.
why: Refresh and capacitor walls (no stored charge to leak), using only Si, N and Al; density comes from stacking tiers rather than from EUV.

title: Sealed nano-vacuum field-emission switches replace gate-oxide access transistors
idea: Effect: Fowler-Nordheim field emission. Mo nanotips face TiN anodes across a ~5 nm vacuum gap sealed by PECVD SiO2 at 350 C, forming the cell access device. Off-current falls exponentially with no thermionic subthreshold tail and no gate dielectric; field-enhanced tips switch on at ~2-3 V.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3) and dependence on Hf high-k and single-crystal silicon; all steps are below 400 C.

title: Prussian-blue ion-insertion cells electroplated at room temperature
idea: Effect: ion migration and intercalation. K+ moves between a near-zero-strain Fe-hexacyanoferrate open framework and a solid electrolyte, changing the Fe3+/Fe2+ ratio and the conductance of a three-terminal channel. The film is electrodeposited from water at 25 C, and its battery-grade fast ion kinetics allow sub-us switching.
why: Scarce-element and thermal-budget intensity: memory made from Fe, C, N and K; zero-strain lattice targets very high cycle life; no vacuum tools for the active layer.

title: Piezoelectric AlN nano-relays give zero-leakage access and end refresh
idea: Effect: the converse piezoelectric effect. A c-axis AlN bimorph sputtered at 300 C bends to close a Mo/TiN nano-contact, so the access device is a mechanical switch with an air-gap off-state and exactly zero subthreshold leakage. Retention is limited only by capacitor dielectric leakage (hours).
why: Refresh energy and bandwidth (fact 3) largely gone; AlN needs no scandium, no Si channel and no thermal budget above 400 C.

title: Cu2O and SnO p-channel oxides put full CMOS periphery above arrays
idea: Effect: dispersive hole bands, from Cu 3d-O 2p hybridization in Cu2O and Sn 5s lone-pair mixing in SnO, give 1-5 cm2/Vs hole mobility. Sputtered at <=300 C and paired with n-type ZTO, they make complementary oxide decoders and drivers stacked over the array instead of beside it.
why: Periphery ~49% of die (fact 7): die area ~-35% and bits per wafer ~+50%, so less single-crystal Si (quartz, poly) per bit; Cu and Sn are abundant.

title: Intercalated multilayer graphene wordlines grown by nickel-mediated precipitation
idea: Effect: charge-transfer intercalation doping. Carbon diffuses through a Ni film at ~350 C and precipitates as multilayer graphene in trenches (layer exchange). FeCl3 intercalation then shifts the Fermi level and cuts resistivity toward Cu, giving barrier-free, electromigration-proof wordlines made of carbon.
why: Tungsten (China ~80%) and WF6; no liner volume at 10-15 nm and abundant feedstock, all below 400 C.

title: Electrophoretic BaTiO3 nanocube monolayers form high-k capacitors cold
idea: Effect: electrophoresis plus size-dependent permittivity. 15 nm BaTiO3 nanocubes, already crystallized by hydrothermal synthesis at ~200 C, drift under DC bias into trenches or pores and pack face to face. An ALD AlOx infill at 250 C seals pinholes, giving k ~100-300 with no 700 C perovskite anneal.
why: Hf/Zr-free route to the k~70 the capacitor wall needs (fact 1); Ba and Ti are widely sourced; nothing exceeds 250 C.

title: Cobalt-free Fe-B/MgO tunnel junctions crystallized under 350 C
idea: Effect: interfacial perpendicular anisotropy from Fe 3d-O 2p hybridization at the Fe/MgO interface. Drop Co entirely and use Mg or Al boron-sink caps instead of Ta/W, so Fe-B free and reference layers crystallize from the MgO template at <=350 C while keeping TMR >150%.
why: Cobalt (DRC ~70%), Ta and W removed from MRAM working-memory stacks; anneal stays inside the 400 C budget.

title: Deuterium kinetic-isotope passivation trims the leakage tail at 400 C
idea: Effect: the kinetic isotope effect. Si-D bonds at access-transistor interfaces and STI corners desorb 10-50x slower than Si-H because the heavier isotope couples to Si phonons. A final 400 C high-pressure D2 anneal, or a deuterated SiN cap, keeps tail traps passivated, suppressing the trap-assisted tunneling that sets refresh.
why: Leakage tail (fact 3): 2-4x longer tail retention halves refresh energy; deuterium comes from abundant water.

title: High-chi block copolymers plus vapor infiltration draw 12 nm arrays
idea: Effect: thermodynamic microphase separation. A high-chi block copolymer anneals at <=250 C into 12-20 nm hexagonal dots or lines, guided by a coarse ArF graphoepitaxial template. Sequential infiltration synthesis (TMA/H2O at 90 C) turns one block into an AlOx hard mask for array etches.
why: EUV chokepoint and PFAS-containing photoacid generators: 3-5 array EUV exposures replaced, with every step <=250 C.

title: Remote-plasma atomic-oxygen oxidation retires quartz furnaces at 400 C
idea: Effect: radical-driven oxidation kinetics. Atomic oxygen from a microwave or ICP remote plasma oxidizes and nitrides silicon at 300-400 C with near-thermal interface quality (Dit ~1e10/cm2eV). Gate, liner and isolation oxides come from single-wafer chambers instead of 900 C batch furnaces.
why: Quartz consumables (furnace tubes, boats, liners) and furnace energy; enables a furnace-free fab under the 400 C ceiling.

title: Surface-activated room-temperature bonding stacks memory layers without solder
idea: Effect: dangling-bond covalent adhesion. An argon fast-atom beam strips native oxides so Cu-Cu and SiO2-SiO2 surfaces fuse at room temperature in vacuum, stacking thinned DRAM or oxide-memory layers at <1 um pitch with no Sn-Ag microbumps, underfill or 400 C bonding anneal.
why: HBM TSV/microbump tax (fact 6), Ag/Sn and fluorinated underfills; denser vertical links at room temperature.

title: Idle LCD panel fabs print multi-tier oxide memory on glass
idea: Effect: wide-bandgap suppression of intrinsic carrier generation (n_i ~ exp(-Eg/2kT)) gives oxide transistors minutes-long retention even at 1 um rules. Retool idle Gen-8.5 LCD lines, which already run <=350 C oxide TFT processes with i-line litho, to stack 8 tiers of 2T0C gain cells on 5.5 m2 glass, about 0.7 TB per panel.
why: Capital intensity and EUV/fab lead time (3-5 yr): uses existing depreciated panel capacity, no EUV and no CZ wafers; at ~$1.5k/m2 for 8 tiers that is ~$12/GB for a CXL warm tier.

title: Zinc-magnesium-oxide ferroelectric tunnel junctions sputtered at room temperature
idea: Effect: polarization-modulated tunnel electroresistance. Wurtzite Zn(1-x)Mg(x)O (x~0.3) is ferroelectric as-deposited at room temperature; a 3-5 nm layer between asymmetric electrodes (TiN / n-ZnO) makes a tunnel junction whose barrier height follows the polarization, so a small read current senses the state without switching it.
why: Hf/Zr-free ferroelectric memory with non-destructive read (fact 8); Zn is abundant and Mg can come from seawater; the process stays near room temperature.
